transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-25
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Michael Torres (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Lucas Green (Redwood CSM); Olivia Martin (Product), Derek Huang (ML Eng), Sofia Ramos (Security), Raj Patel (Data)

[00:00] Michael Torres: hey everyone thanks for joining, can you hear me ok?
[00:07] Olivia Martin: yes loud and clear, thanks Michael
[00:12] Priya Desai: good afternoon all, i'll kick us off with the quality dashboard highlights then we'll dig into the regression cases
[00:20] Derek Huang: quick note — we're on EMEA hours here but timing works, thanks

Summary & context:
[00:30] Priya Desai: so last week we pushed prompt-set v3 with two changes: adjusted negative prompts to reduce hallucinations and switched to model-variant A (smaller param count, aggressive quant). overall we saw a small lift in latency but a regression in one of your scoring buckets — specifically factual_accuracy dropped from 92% to about 88 on the dev set.
[01:05] Olivia Martin: right and the regression showed up mostly on our finance domain Q&A prompts, like benefit eligibility questions where it invented providers names
[01:18] Raj Patel: to add, our internal scoring flagged hallucinations up 3x for long-form answers > 150 tokens

Triage & investigation:
[01:35] Priya Desai: we dug into logs; looks like the quantized path for variant A had slightly degraded attention behavior on long contexts — it's a tradeoff we often see when moving to 4-bit quant, especially with some of the custom attention kernels. sometimes the KV-cache alignment differs.
[02:00] Derek Huang: is that consistent with what Redwood Dedicated would do if we moved to a different kernel or compilation flag?
[02:08] Priya Desai: good question — Dedicated gives us more control over compilation flags and we can force a fallback kernel that is higher fidelity but costs more cycles. on hosted we typically choose the cost/latency sweet spot.
[02:22] Michael Torres: so option A: revert to float16 model-variant for those prompts; option B: keep quantized but add guardrail and reweight prompt scoring; option C: test dedicated kernel fallback for the problematic routes

On metrics and scoring:
[02:40] Priya Desai: current metrics in the dashboard — accuracy/factuality is our main KPI, plus hallucination rate (manual label), avg_token_loss, and BLEU-ish similarity for templated answers. we also track latency p50/p95 and cost-per-1k-tokens.
[02:55] Olivia Martin: our SLA is more about correctness than latency, but we want sub-300ms p95 ideally for short answers
[03:05] Michael Torres: noted — we'll prioritize factuality for your prioritized route set

Example transcript snippets and annotation notes:
[03:20] Priya Desai: here's a sample from last night's run — prompt ID 4487: 'Which providers cover prenatal counseling under plan X?' Model returned: 'PrimeHealth and NovaCare cover prenatal counseling under plan X' — both are fabricated. labeled as hallucination.
[03:42] Derek Huang: we pushed 200 labeled examples of that pattern last week; why still happening?
[03:47] Priya Desai: possible causes: model underfitting for the domain due to quantization, or prompt template variance. also scoring thresholds for guardrails may be too permissive.

Discussion on guardrails and threshold tuning:
[04:10] Michael Torres: for guardrails we recommend three layers: 1) pre-response intent classifier to route high-risk prompts to a high-fidelity model, 2) post-response LLM critic + string match checks for protected tokens, 3) conservative fallback to safe-response or escalation to human.
[04:30] Sofia Ramos: on the security side we need audit logs for any fallback, plus proof that PII is not leaked by the critic — can we include audit log IDs in the response trace?
[04:40] Priya Desai: yes Redwood Console already surfaces token-level traces and we can tag request IDs; for Private deployments audit logs can be stored in your S3 bucket or via your KMS. we'll follow up with SOC2 doc links.

Hands-on debugging notes:
[05:05] Priya Desai: i ran two experiments overnight: A) revert to float16 on the same model arch, B) keep quant but increase prompt_prefix specificity and tighten hallucination threshold. float16 fixed the factuality drop to 93.5 but increased p95 latency ~22ms. tightening prompt helped but only reduced hallucination by ~1.5 points.
[05:35] Michael Torres: so float16 is best for quality but cost/latency tradeoff — Derek how do you feel about that?
[05:43] Derek Huang: quality-first makes sense initially for pilot; we can optimize cost later. maybe do canary on 10% of traffic with float16?
[05:52] Lucas Green: we can also schedule a dedicated kernel fallback for just that route which might get us float16-like fidelity without full cost increase — depends on how the kernels perform on your workload.

Decisions and routing policy:
[06:10] Michael Torres: agreed next plan — run 1k-sample regression with float16 model on the prioritized prompt set, add stricter guardrail thresholds for long-form answers, and run a dedicated kernel latency test for the route.

Benchmarks and artifacts referenced:
[06:30] Priya Desai: shared benchmark spreadsheet: https://drive.redwood/example-benchmarks (note: link placeholder) — it has per-prompt results, latency histograms and cost calc. also attached the prompt-set v3 and v3a (with narrower prefix) in the sheet.
[06:55] Olivia Martin: thanks, we'll load the sheet into our tracker

Security / compliance notes:
[07:05] Sofia Ramos: we need SOC2 report, SAML SSO integration spec, and confirmation that audit logs include request/response IDs and KMS key usage. is Redwood Private required for storing logs in our VPC?
[07:22] Michael Torres: you can do Redwood Hosted and stream audit logs to your S3 via a private connector, but for air-gapped or on-prem storage Private is recommended. we'll send SOC2 and SAML docs in the follow-up.

Open questions from customer:
[07:45] Derek Huang: how deterministic are the guardrails? if we add a post-critic it'll increase latency — is there an async path?
[07:55] Priya Desai: yes you can do async critic for non-blocking ops; for high-risk queries we recommend sync critic or model fallback, otherwise async batch checks for logging and metric collection.

Regression examples walk-through:
[08:20] Priya Desai: walking through 6 representative regression examples now — note timestamps in sheet for each example. example 2 is interesting because it fails only when context > 600 tokens; otherwise ok.
[08:40] Raj Patel: that aligns with our observation that long context answers are where hallucinations spike

Customer constraints and timeline:
[09:00] Olivia Martin: timeline remains end of April for pilot completion, with exec review 1st week of May. success criteria: <2% hallucination on priority set, p95 latency < 350ms for short prompts, and security checklist completed.
[09:20] Michael Torres: sounds good, we can align.

Pricing & cost discussion (brief):
[09:30] Michael Torres: we discussed cost per 1k tokens — dedicated kernel fallback and float16 will raise unit cost. we'll include per-route cost estimates in the spreadsheet.
[09:40] Olivia Martin: send that please

Wrap-up and next steps:
[10:00] Michael Torres: recap — Redwood will: 1) send updated prompt-set and scoring sheet, 2) run 1k float16 regression and share results, 3) prepare canary config for variant A quant and dedicated kernel test, 4) share SOC2 and SAML docs. Customer will provide anonymized error examples and confirm security requirements.
[10:25] Derek Huang: i'll get the 50 error cases together and drop them in the sheet
[10:30] Sofia Ramos: i'll review the SOC2 items and email requirements
[10:40] Priya Desai: we'll aim to have benchmark results by 2025-03-28 and schedule the dedicated latency run for the week of 2025-03-31
[10:50] Michael Torres: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with notes and the sheet — talk soon

Notes on transcription quality: some speaker attribution may be off; product names sometimes transcribed as 'Redwood Dedicated' -> 'Redwood dedic' or 'Redwood dedik' in raw export.

References shared: benchmark spreadsheet (Drive link), prompt-set v3 (sheet tab), SOC2 link (will be shared in follow-up), canary config template (in repo).
